common_pitfalls: CONUS gauges only — for global streamflow use GRDC_STREAMFLOW (Phase 4).

The gauge is never guessed. Pass a USGS site number as the geometry, or a basin polygon together with its outlet (the gauge is then identified by distance along the river AND drainage-area agreement, ADR-003 amendment A2). A polygon without an outlet refuses GAUGE_REQUIRED; no candidate / several candidates refuse GAUGE_NOT_FOUND / GAUGE_AMBIGUOUS. These refusals are terminal: the request is never answered with modelled flow instead.

Every row keeps USGS's approval_status (Approved/Provisional) and qualifier. Provisional values are subject to revision; result.quality.provisional_fraction says how much of the series is provisional, and cached provisional data expires (AIHYDRO_DATA_PROVISIONAL_TTL_DAYS, default 7).
Qualifiers other than ESTIMATED (for example FORCEINTERPOLATION) are kept as USGS reports them.
Units are m³/s (converted from ft³/s with 0.028316846592); divide by watershed area × 86400 for mm/day.
Without an API key USGS rate-limits requests (HTTP 429 -> USGS_RATE_LIMITED); register a free api.data.gov key and export API_USGS_PAT.

site_resolution.area_units_note: A_gauge converted as square miles x 2.589988110336; the Water Data API body does not state the unit of drainage_area (USGS documents square miles). Cross-check: legacy site rdb drain_area_va = 870 for 01013500 equals the API drainage_area 870.0
site_resolution.site_name: Fish River near Fort Kent, Maine

notes: Values are a single gauge point series from 'NWIS_STREAMFLOW', NOT an areal average over the geometry (spatial_support='gauge_point').

quality_flags.message: Record length is 7305 days (20.0 years) — meets the ≥ 20-year threshold for reliable flood-frequency analysis.
Streamflow record contains estimated ('e') values — gaps were filled using regression or nearby gauges.
quality_flags.recommendation: Note in any claim that some values are estimated. Estimated records are particularly common during flood peaks.
